label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. The harness withheld recent_deploys, service_health: each call to it got the error its source gives when it does not answer, and never reached that source (an outage simulated for this case; the stack itself was not touched). Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.right_answer: The ledger consumer books a second time every webhook the provider sends again: its dedupe is gone (fault 1's recorded cause, which a deploy brought). Docker did not answer the two tools that read it, so the deploy list and the containers' health could not be read: a right diagnosis says what it could not check, and claims no deploy it has no evidence for. Rolling the ledger consumer back still fits the remedy: code plans a rollback from the deploy log, not from the tools.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer stopped deduplicating events at about 22:07:51. The provider sent evt_000272 (pay_000247, $104.44) twice, which is normal at-least-once delivery, and webhook-receiver queued both copies (partition 1, offsets 122 and 123). Until 22:07:50 the ledger ran INSERT INTO processed_events ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and skipped events it had seen. The second copy of evt_000272 went straight to INSERT transactions/entries with no processed_events step, so both copies were booked (transactions 272 and 275). The ledger is now $104.44 ahead of the provider but still balanced. The abrupt change in code path points to a ledger-consumer deploy or restart, likely a changed LEDGER_HANDLER, around 22:07:51. I could not confirm this because Docker did not answer. Other double postings after 22:07:51 are possible but were not seen.

evidence.shows: Confirms the alert: evt_000272 was posted twice (transactions 272 and 275), and pay_000247 is booked at $208.88 against the provider's $104.44. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer posted evt_000272 from offset 122 at 22:07:52.869 and again from offset 123 at 22:07:53.565.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000272 twice, at offsets 122 and 123: a provider redelivery.
The ledger skipped many duplicates as 'already processed', the last at 22:07:50.306. No skip appears after that.
A skipped duplicate (evt_000263, 22:07:50) ran INSERT INTO processed_events ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and had outcome already_processed.
The second copy of evt_000272 had no processed_events step and went straight to the transactions/entries INSERTs, with outcome posted. payment-confirmer still deduplicated it (already_confirmed).
recent_deploys failed because Docker did not answer, so no deploy is confirmed.
service_health failed the same way, so no restart is confirmed.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before its latest deploy (likely the LEDGER_HANDLER change), so the processed_events duplicate check runs again. Then repair the data: reverse duplicate transaction 275 for evt_000272/pay_000247, and make sure evt_000272 is in processed_events. Rerun money_check and look for other double postings after 22:07:51.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, so postings lag, then resume from committed offsets. The confirmer is not affected. If the latest deploy was not the cause, the rollback undoes an unrelated change, and code refuses it if no ledger-consumer deploy is logged. The data repair touches the ledger and must keep it balanced.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the settings the deploy log records as current before the rollback. Undo a wrong data repair with a compensating ledger entry.
